Ben Cline Reintroduces Legislation to Increase Opportunities for Veterans Jul 22 Press Releases Cline Amendment Passes in NDAA Stay Connected Meet Ben Ben Cline represents Virginia’s 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he is a member of the House Committee on the Judiciary, the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on the Budget. He previously served as a Member of the Virginia House of Delegates, representing the 24th District from 2002-2018. In the Virginia House, Cline chaired the Committee on Militia, Police, and Public Safety. learn more key issues Fighting For Our Veterans Finding Energy Solutions Growing The Economy Fixing Our Healthcare System

Health | U.S. Representative Ben Cline Fixing Our Healthcare System</h2> <p>Virginia’s Sixth Congressional District is blessed to be the home of several of the top 10 hospitals in the Commonwealth of Virginia. From Carilion in Roanoke to Valley Health in Winchester, Virginia’s hospitals are vital to the health and well-being of Sixth District residents.</p> <p>With the rise in premiums and deductibles and the ever-increasing cost of prescription drugs, Congressman Cline has made it a priority to address America’s healthcare issues using effective, free-market solutions, while protecting patients with preexisting conditions. He has also worked to advance legislation to combat the COVID-19 pandemic, which has had a devastating impact on the United States.</p> <p>Congressman Cline believes it is a priority that Congress foster affordability and accessibility in the healthcare marketplace in a way that both parties can endorse and that is consistent with the entrepreneurial spirit of our nation.</p> <p>Below are just a few examples of pieces of legislation Congressman Cline has supported during his tenure to accomplish these goals:<br /> </p> <h3>119th Congress:</h3> <div> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 317</strong>, the Healthcare Freedom Act of 2025, would allow anyone to hold a Health Freedom Account to allow for greater flexibility and personalization of healthcare decisions.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>H.R. 1262,&nbsp;</strong>the Give Kids a Chance Act, which focuses on accelerating pediatric cancer treatments and improving drug development for childhood diseases.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>H.R. 3164</strong>, the Ensuring Community Access to Pharmacist Services Act, would allow Medicare Part B to pay for certain services provided by pharmacists, making key services like testing, treating illnesses, and administering vaccinations more accessible.&nbsp;</li> </ul> </div> <ul></ul> <h3>118th Congress:</h3> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 497</strong>, the Freedom for Health Care Workers Act ends the Biden Administration’s COVID-19 vaccine mandate for healthcare worker

Growing the Economy | U.S. Representative Ben Cline Congressman Cline is focused on growing the economy and keeping more money in the pockets of hard-working Americans. The Congressman is fighting to reduce the regulatory burden on businesses and employees and is also committed to lowering taxes that stunt economic growth. He also believes in promoting free trade agreements and policies that benefit farmers and small businesses in Virginia’s Sixth Congressional District.</p> <p>Below are just a few examples of pieces of legislation Congressman Cline has supported during his tenure to accomplish these goals:<br /> </p> <h2>119th Congress:</h2> <div> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 1</strong>, the Working Families Tax Plan, made permanent certain tax provisions from the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, preventing the largest tax hike on American workers in history.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>H.R. 3174</strong>, the Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act, which expands capital access for small manufacturers, and the bipartisan Office of Rural Affairs Enhancement Act, which bolsters resources for rural small businesses.&nbsp;<br /> </li> </ul> </div> <ul></ul> <h2>118th Congress:</h2> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 358</strong>, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act requires federal regulators to assess the full economic effects of proposed regulations on small businesses and consider alternative measures to reduce burdens before they act.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 23</strong>, the Family and Small Business Taxpayer Protection Act rescinds all new IRS funding for squeezing middle-class families and small businesses, while enhancing the services Americans expect to receive from their government.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 3400</strong>, the Small Businesses Before Bureaucrats Act updates the 1958 jurisdictional standards of the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) to reflect modern revenue levels and ensure that such standards accurately represent the size of the economy each year.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 277</strong> the REINS Act updates the 1958 jurisdict

Energy | U.S. Representative Ben Cline Energy Policy</h2> <p>With the abundance of energy sources right here in the Commonwealth, Congressman Cline supports an “all of the above” energy policy. Therefore, Congressman Cline believes in supporting policies that serve to bolster both American security and economic interests, and also safeguard our natural resources in a responsible manner that does not jeopardize Virginia’s energy jobs or burdens Virginia’s families with high energy costs.</p> <p>Below are just a few examples of pieces of legislation Congressman Cline has supported during his tenure to accomplish these goals:<br /> </p> <h3>119th Congress:</h3> <div> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 1</strong>, the Working Families Tax Plan, included provisions to end harmful tax credits for wind and solar projects that were driving up electricity prices.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>H.R. 26</strong>, the Protecting American Energy Production Act, which prohibits the president from implementing a federal moratorium on fracking, which protects and encourages domestic oil and natural gas production.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>H.R. 1047</strong>, the GRID Power Act, which gives regional transmission organizations the authority to prioritize energy projects that can provide stable, baseload power to improve grid reliability and lower costs.&nbsp;<br /> </li> </ul> </div> <ul></ul> <h3>118th Congress:</h3> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 1</strong>, the Lower Energy Costs Act restores America’s energy independence and reduce costs by: increasing domestic energy production; cutting burdensome government red tape; and reforming the permitting process.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 21</strong>, the Strategic Production Response Act limits the drawdown of petroleum in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) until the Department of Energy (DOE) submits to Congress a plan to increase the percentage of federal lands leased for oil and gas production.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 1067</strong>, the American Energy Act helps reduce the backlog at the Bureau of Land Management by extending the

Veterans | U.S. Representative Ben Cline SUPPORTING VETERANS</h2> <p>As a Member of Congress, advocating for veterans and their families is a top priority for Congressman Cline. His district offices help veterans with their claims with the Department of Veterans Affairs, and in Washington, he is always looking for new ways to do more to support those who supported us.</p> <p>Throughout his tenure, Congressman Cline has strived to honor veterans by advocating for and passing legislation, some of which has been signed into law, that deals with burn pits, suicide prevention, veteran health care options, blue water navy, the widow’s tax, reserve and national guard bankruptcy, and opening up membership into the American Legion for previously disqualified veterans.</p> <h2>118th Congress:</h2> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 4366</strong>, the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act of FY24 which provides funding for Defense Department military and family housing construction activities and remediation at closed military bases. Reforming Congress | U.S. Representative Ben Cline Congress and Transparency</h2> <p>Congress was established through Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution, and as such, our Founding Fathers put the utmost responsibility in lawmakers to uphold their inalienable rights. Sadly, today’s Congress has become overreaching and dysfunctional. Congressman Cline is committed to serving the constituents of Virginia’s Sixth Congressional District by ensuring Congress has the necessary transparency and procedural ability to accomplish meaningful reform.</p> <p>Below are just a few examples of pieces of legislation Congressman Cline has supported during his tenure to accomplish these goals:</p> <h3>118th Congress:</h3> <ul> <li><strong>H.Res. 96</strong>, the Transparency in Federal Spending Resolution permits Members to object to the consideration of legislation that authorizes or appropriates funding for programs unless the legislation includes a table that details the funding.</li> </ul> <h3>117th Congress:</h3> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 872</strong>, the One Subject at a Time Act attempts to end the practice of including more than one subject in a single bill by requiring that each bill enacted by Congress be limited to only one subject.</li> </ul> <h3>116th Congress:</h3> <ul> <li><strong>H.R. 3403</strong>, the Searchable Legislation Act of 2019 establishes a baseline that all bills, resolutions, and documents of Congress be created and stored in a manner that is electronically searchable which would increase transparency.</li> <li><strong>H.R. 3402</strong>, the Readable Legislation Act of 2019 requires that bills are written in a manner that shows the entire section of code it is amending, which would increase comprehensive knowledge of the effects of the legislation.</li> </ul> For more information concerning work and views related to Reforming Congress, please <a href="/contact">contact our office.</a>" /> Skip to Content Reforming Congress Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email Congress and Transparency Congress was established thro
